title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Stop waiting and complaining; lead yourself and build the work you deserve
summary: Andreea Popa writes a personal essay about spending three years in work that didn't fit, mistaking inaction for patience and complaint for progress. She argues people hold the pen on their own careers and should invest in skills, network, narrative and standards. Cris Pop is not mentioned; the views and anecdotes are the author's.

principles.text: Patience can become a story that justifies staying still; the price of waiting is only seen after it is paid.
principles.quote: But sometimes, patience becomes the story we tell ourselves to justify staying still.

principles.text: Complaining without action is procrastination that feels productive; real change requires risk.
principles.quote: But complaining without action is just another form of procrastination, a way to avoid the truth that change requires risk.

principles.text: Lead yourself first: shift from asking why it happens to you to asking what you can do about it.
principles.quote: Not "Why is this happening to me?", but "What can I do about this?"

principles.text: Invest in what you control (skills, network, narrative, standards) without waiting for permission.
principles.quote: You don’t need permission to grow.

principles.text: Don't bend yourself to fit every opportunity; look for environments that fit you.
principles.quote: You don’t have to adjust yourself to fit every opportunity. Start looking for the ones that fit you.

principles.text: Change is built from small, consistent actions, starting with what you can carry today.
principles.quote: It's built from small, consistent actions taken by someone who decided they deserved better.
